q: Why does Socket Mode let the Slack bot work without being publicly reachable?
options: It listens on a public webhook endpoint
The bot opens an outbound WebSocket connection to Slack
It tunnels through a public proxy automatically
Slack hosts the bot for you
explanation: Socket Mode uses outbound WebSockets, so the agent only needs to open a connection to Slack — no inbound/public access required.

q: Which two tokens does a Slack connection require?
options: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_APP_TOKEN
SLACK_API_KEY and SLACK_SECRET
SLACK_WEBHOOK and SLACK_AUTH
SLACK_TOKEN and SLACK_ID
explanation: You need the bot token (xoxb-) and the app token (xapp-), plus SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS.

q: What does SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS do in this setup?
options: Sets the default language of the bot
Names the channels the bot joins automatically
Restricts who can use the agent to listed Slack Member IDs
Defines the bot's display name
explanation: It's the safety gate — only the listed Member IDs (like U01ABC2DEF3) can use the agent.

q: In Discord server channels, when does Hermes respond by default?
options: To every message, no matter what
Only when it is @mentioned
Only in the first channel of the server
Only during business hours
explanation: By default Hermes responds only when @mentioned in server channels; you can make specific channels mention-free with DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS.

q: Which of these is a true statement about Slack channels?
options: The bot auto-joins every channel on install
You must invite the bot with /invite to add it to a channel
The bot can only work in DMs, not channels
Classic Slack apps are the recommended approach in 2025
explanation: The bot will not auto-join; you invite it with /invite @Hermes Agent. Classic apps were deprecated in March 2025.
